thread.title: Amazon was almost worth $1 trillion, but it is down $119 billion in just two trading sessions

author: QEF Team
title: Amazon was almost worth $1 trillion, but it is down $119 billion in just two trading sessions
text:
Amazon was almost worth $1 trillion, but it is down $119 billion in just two trading sessions By 20 views
Amazon.com Inc. was very nearly the second U.S. company worth $1 trillion last month. Now, it’s worth less than a neighbor and major cloud rival.
Amazon AMZN, -0.55% had been No. 2 to Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.50% and briefly flirted with a $1 trillion market cap in early September , but a steep descent since releasing earnings last week has chopped off nearly $120 billion from its valuation in just the past two trading sessions. Combined with an October tech-stock swoon that had already knocked it back from striking distance of $1 trillion and left the e-commerce powerhouse trailing the tech company on the other side of Lake Washington, Microsoft Corp. MSFT, -0.12% .
Before reporting earnings Thursday after the markets closed, Amazon finished the session with a valuation of $871.5 billion, using current share counts. As of the end of Monday’s session — which saw Amazon stock fall 6.3% and wrap up its worst two-session stretch since February 2014 — Amazon was worth $752.5 billion, while Microsoft stood at $797.2 FactSet calculations. FactSet
Amazon was actually closer to the tech giant trailing it, Google parent company Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, +1.43% GOOG, +1.58% at $714.5 billion, than Microsoft. The stock has declined 23.2% in October through Monday’s close, while the S&P 500 index SPX, +1.57% has declined 9.4% for the month.
On back-to-back days last week, Microsoft and Amazon promised investors at least 10% revenue growth for the fourth quarter. Microsoft was rewarded after its report , but Amazon’s forecast of 10%-to-20% growth represented a significant decline from the 30% revenue growth it reported for the third quarter.

Amazon may have been cautious in its forecast. “Much of our, not only our revenue for the quarter, but also for the year, comes in that very tight window between the middle of November and the end of the year, so it’s always a very difficult period for us to estimate,” Chief Financial Officer Brian Olsavsky said Thursday afternoon in an earnings call.
Amazon had a legitimate accounting excuse, as well. Amazon Prime subscription fees were “tilted” to the fourth quarter every year until 2018, Olsavsky said, when Amazon stretched that total across the year. With 100 million customers now paying an increased $120 subscription price , that’s a big chunk of money that disappears out of this holiday season’s sales figures.
Apple became the first company to top the $1 trillion barrier in August , winning a footrace with Amazon, and has maintained the milestone even through the tech bloodbath, ending Monday with a market valuation of $1.025 trillion. Several analysts expect Microsoft to eventually top $1 trillion as it continues to successfully battle Amazon in cloud computing while enjoying gains in cloud software and its legacy personal-computer business, but more believe Amazon will get there.
Microsoft’s share price would need to top $130 at current shares-outstanding levels to reach $1 trillion. A dozen analysts have share-price targets for Microsoft of $130 or higher; the average price target of more than 30 analysts tracked by FactSet as of Friday morning was $125.69.
Amazon would need to top $2,045 a share to approach a $1 trillion valuation at its current share count. After the e-commerce leader’s earnings report, the average price target on its stock from more than 40 analysts tracking the company was $2,183.67.
